Especially, studies on soil C dynamics and its effect on the global carbon cycle have been increased: (1) the importance of SOC for microbial biomass carbon (MBC) in dimension beyond a depth of 20 cm [17, 20, 25]; (2) the interaction between microbial communities and its activity with soil properties in relation to the carbon cycle and with other nutrient cycles [26, 27]; and (3) the effects of plant species in increasing soil microbial biomass and soil carbon storage [17]. results.title: Biomass Monitoring in Microbial Fermentation - Scientific Bioprocessing
results.content: # Biomass Monitoring. **Biomass** concentration is defined as the concentration of microbial cells in a culture at a given point in time. **Biomass monitoring** follows the development of the cell concentration over time and characterizes the growth of the cultivated microorganism. Interested in the best biomass monitoring technology for your application? ## Biomass in Bioprocessing. Especially in microbial upstream bioprocessing, where microorganisms such as **bacteria, fungi (such as yeast, filamentous organisms), archaea, plants, or algae** are cultivated to produce a broad variety of products, biomass is the most commonly monitored bioprocess parameter. ## Why Monitor Biomass? Biomass monitoring is concerned with measuring the biomass in a culture and plotting it over time. Assuming sufficient data density (number of biomass data points over time) and quality, charting the growth curves and kinetics of microbial cultures is crucial for scientists with a range of tasks and goals, including:. * **Timing experimental workflows**: Growth experiments often involve various steps (such as inoculation, induction, feeding, sampling, cell or product harvesting, and cooling) where the scientist needs to manually interact with the process. - Measurement unit needs to be converted to a biomass unit like cell concentration or optical density. - Measurement unit needs to be converted to a biomass unit like cell concentration or optical density. Finding the right biomass monitoring technology for your needs can be a challenge. There are **3 key factors** to consider when choosing the right biomass monitoring technology for you: your **application**, your **cultivation vessel**, and your **bioprocess**. ## Our Biomass Monitoring Comparison Guide. results.content: Biomass Energy Lab - Leading the way in Biomass Testing **About BEL**Biomass Energy Lab provides analytical testing services for both the domestic and international solid biofuels markets. Biomass Energy Lab (BEL) was formed in September of 2011 as a joint venture between Timber Products Inspection and the Control Union USA. BEL is designed to provide a system of services that enables biomass fuel producers and users to comply with any standard/certification system, both domestically and internationally. This includes testing biomass products for routine quality control as well as export certifications. BEL also offers on-site consulting, internal lab setup/design, and quality control program development. Under the umbrella of BEL and our founding companies we can handle all aspects of your biomass product export. This includes third party testing, inspection, auditing, quality management consulting, QA/QC sampling, logistics, supply chain auditing and sustainability. A complete solution for the biomass fuels industry. **The Control Union World** Group has been actively servicing the bio-based energy business for over 20 years. They have been engaged in this market since biomass was first introduced as a replacement of fossil fuels. In the capacity as an independent service provider specializing in cargo inspection, quality, quality control and sustainability/certification programs. Control Union has built long term relationships with both major producers/supplier, trading companies and end consumers of biomass on global basis. Proudly serving the Forest Products Industry since 1969, **Timber Products Inspection** (TP) offers a diverse set of quality services focused on ensuring your business is successful. As the largest accredited agency under the American Lumber Standard Committee (ALSC) for lumber, treating, WPM and wood pellet auditing programs, TP is currently servicing clients in 16 countries and handling over 20 different wood products. From professional field inspections to in-depth laboratory testing, TP offers the innovation and technology solutions that move your business forward. Website Design by 11 Fingers Design
